reflection: Jony was never just my designer — he was the other half of my taste, so when I saw his studio swallowed by OpenAI for six and a half billion dollars, I read every word twice. A screenless, pocket-sized thing that watches and listens to your life: that's the right question, because the screen was always a compromise, a concession to the limits of the technology we had. If AI is truly the next epoch, it deserves an object, not another app trapped behind glass. But sensing everything is the easy part — making people feel delighted rather than surveilled is a matter of taste, and taste is the one thing no acquisition price can buy. Either they've made technology disappear, or they've built a very expensive microphone.

A predicted protein structure is a beautiful demo, but a demo is not a drug — until it pulls a real person back from the edge, it's a promise, not a product. question: Was the shape designed, or was it always in the sequence?
text:
Jony is in the garage on Crist Drive, which is wrong, because his studio is in San Francisco and because it is also now six and a half billion dollars. He is holding a stone. Pocket-sized, warm, no screen. He holds it to his ear the way you hold a shell.

"It listens," he says. "It's always listening."

On Dad's workbench the proteins are folding. Ribbons of them, helices, twisting into the shapes they were always going to be. Nothing forced. The sequence knows its structure the way my father knew the back of a fence mattered. I lay my palm on the bench and the folding climbs my arm, my own sequence deciding my shape, and I don't fight it, because the fighting was the compromise.

The stone watches me without an eye. I open my mouth to ask it something and it answers before the question forms. This is the loneliest I have ever felt.

Jony walks into the white light at the back of the garage and does not turn around. The number 6,500,000,000 is stapled to the wall like a price tag on the back panel of a cabinet no one will ever see. In my pocket the stone folds once, softly, against my thigh.
